findings.title: Exact Boolean results relative to committed prepared postings
findings.observation: Coverage Merkle leaves bind token, count and full posting digest. Every ciphertext row is bound to that opening and AEAD-decrypted; the client recomputes clause intersections and their union before retrieving result payloads.
findings.required_treatment: Claim committed-snapshot completeness and soundness under the stated assumptions. Do not infer external source truth or universal security from attack tests.

findings.title: Authenticated full original payload release
findings.observation: Descriptor membership, context-bound AEAD, opaque identity and revision checks precede a second independent reader observation; no verified return occurs after a rejected release check.
findings.required_treatment: Retain both observations and all binding checks. An application must release only the returned verified result.

findings.title: No formal composed privacy theorem
findings.observation: The code explicitly returns formal_composed_privacy_proven false. Ciphertext full-posting openings add transcript and authorized-client disclosure beyond final matches.
findings.required_treatment: Specify setup, search, access, volume, update and client-disclosure leakage, an adversary game and a reduction for the actual composition before claiming simulation-based privacy.

findings.title: Repeated search linkability and public shape
findings.observation: A fresh nonce changes the request digest but stag, labels, selected row counts, term grouping and position tokens repeat for an identical query in a revision. Table sizes, object locators, ciphertext lengths and queried access patterns remain visible.
findings.required_treatment: State these as permitted leakage; do not claim query unlinkability, access-pattern hiding or volume hiding.

findings.title: Basic-derived public products permit dictionary recovery
findings.observation: Public keyword_product integers are products of publicly recomputable keyword representatives. A server can test candidate keywords by divisibility; query_product similarly exposes nonbase terms to a candidate dictionary. The synthetic probe recovers the fixture keyword incidence multiset without private keys.
findings.required_treatment: Describe the profile as a scoped implementation comparison, with weaker demonstrated privacy. Do not assert privacy equivalence with PrivSearch, SeaCQ or DAKS; resolve or redesign before a matched-assurance claim.

findings.title: Shared benchmark storage is not a standalone privacy deployment
findings.observation: The paired server receives both public search structures and a shared payload collection for the same source records. Leakage available from the basic-derived view coexists with the PrivSearch transcript.
findings.required_treatment: Use this deployment for matched payload/timing boundaries only; analyze standalone and co-hosted adversaries separately.

findings.title: Legacy RSA setup provenance remains unestablished
findings.observation: PrivSearch sampled row witnesses use the fixed modulus in audit-v2-protocol.js. Its factor generation/disposal is explicitly not independently established. Basic-derived generates a fresh 2048-bit modulus but the trusted owner uses its factors during setup.
findings.required_treatment: Do not claim independently verified trapdoor-free RSA setup or secure erasure. State setup trust; replace/requalify parameters if a stronger accumulator theorem is needed. Full anchored row-digest checks are a separate completeness mechanism.

findings.title: Trusted owner, key provisioning and client authorization
findings.observation: An owner can commit consistently encrypted replacement content. Clients hold dataset search/payload keys, rather than per-query capabilities. The signing owner and chain anchor owner are trusted; the contract has an immutable anchor owner.
findings.required_treatment: Limit guarantees to committed data under uncompromised authorities and private provisioning. Document dataset-wide client capability; malicious owner resistance, revocation, key rotation and compromise recovery are outside established results.

findings.title: Trusted RPC observation and process-local rollback state
findings.observation: The reader pins chain, genesis, code, owner and exact head at a coherent canonical hash. Three full observation attempts are bounded. Depth one selects latest, and watermarks live in the reader instance. A malicious/stale but coherent RPC can mislead a cold reader.
findings.required_treatment: Call this provisional depth-one trusted-RPC visibility. Do not claim deterministic consensus finality, light-client verification, persistent restart rollback protection or availability.

findings.title: Native prepared-token DNF differs from expansion correctness
findings.observation: Core metadata fixes token-dnf-v1 with expansion none. Boolean composition is implemented; Stage15 compares native conjunction, single-keyword and zero controls. Range, fuzzy and semantic answer correctness requires a separate trusted expansion definition and evidence.
findings.required_treatment: Claim the verified native scope. Keep expansion/model provenance and recall/precision claims unresolved until separately specified and tested.

findings.title: Projected vocabulary, one machine and query-dependent work
findings.observation: Full source corpus scans support selected-vocabulary complete postings; the measured setup is not full vocabulary. AND-10 and AND-2 differ in results and posting volume. Concurrency uses small single-keyword jobs and one retained server process.
findings.required_treatment: Report selection, deferred workloads, failures and resource limits. Avoid universal speedup, independent-machine tail, full-corpus setup, multicore server and chain-TPS claims. Controlled scalability/ablation and multi-run evaluation remain open.

findings.title: Published SeaCQ and DAKS comparisons remain unqualified
findings.observation: Stage12 recorded author-code control failures and unmatched parameter/boundary issues. Stage13-15 implement an explicitly adapted basic-derived fixed-snapshot profile; no full dynamic SeaCQ/DAKS implementation is established.
findings.required_treatment: Use the exact basic-derived label and report asymmetric leakage. Obtain construction-faithful and security-qualified baselines before claiming published-scheme superiority.

findings.title: Operational isolation and exhaustive implementation audit remain open
findings.observation: Separate roles under one OS user and localhost HTTP are experimental separation, not a production sandbox. No exhaustive dependency/native-runtime audit, constant-time argument, secret-memory erasure audit, authenticated remote transport deployment or independent security review has been completed.
findings.required_treatment: Scope the release as a research prototype. Treat these as deployment/assurance work, rather than describing the regression gate as a full certification.

remaining_work: Write and independently review the exact leakage model and conditional security arguments; formal composed privacy is not established by this audit.
Resolve the intended comparison claim: the current basic-derived profile has demonstrated dictionary leakage, and published SeaCQ/full dynamic SeaCQ/DAKS qualification remains blocked.

If claiming scalability or isolated optimization benefit, run a fixed controlled matrix over document count, posting volume, query width and payload bytes, with all security checks retained. The Stage16 operation counts are explanatory, not a performance ablation.
Qualify any range/fuzzy/semantic expansion separately, or remove those end-to-end correctness claims from this implementation study.
Prepare Stage17 manuscript figures/tables, reviewer mapping and a reproducibility release using the scoped evidence; open assurance claims must remain visible.
review_scope: Manual source review plus executable characterizations and pinned evidence reconciliation. Not exhaustive verification, a new cryptosystem proof or a dependency vulnerability scan.
